newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Old Mutual bullish on JSE, eyes banks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Old Mutual bullish on JSE, eyes banks.

text.p: South African financial services giant Old Mutual said on Thursday that the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) was still in a bullish phase and that the banking sector offered especially good prospects.
Adrian Allardice, portfolio manager of Old Mutual Unit Trusts' Industrial Fund, said the second six months of 1997 would still see strong growth for unit trusts investors.
"We are still in a buying phase and investors should do well," he said.
However, investment in gold shares, which have recently dropped to four year lows as bullion suffers a collapse, was to be tempered.
"We remain of the opinion that the gold market is not the place to have a lot of money in," he told reporters.

He said that Old Mutual's generally robust outlook on the JSE came on the back of a better gold and foreign reserves position, improved balance of payments in spite of a lower gold price and expectations of continued falls in inflation.
"We are expecting inflation to fall back at least to below seven percent next year. It could be even better towards the end of the year," he said.

The JSE surged strongly in June and earlier this month to touch an all-time trading high of 8,844.6 on July 3, but has since come off as it suffers from bullion price woes in the gold sector and a shaky local rand and bond markets.

However, Allardice said an expected rate cut later in the year would trigger growth that would flow through in to 1998. "While the market has discounted to some extent prospects of a cut in bank rate and there could be a short-term pullback, we expect specific market sectors to continue to move ahead," he said.
"The bullish scenario is likely to remain in place for some time," he added.
The market is also set to benefit from an upsurge in foreign interest and the relatively painless easing of some foreign exchange controls on individuals.
Allardice said he was cautious on some share ratings in the financial sector, but that banks were looking attractive.

"Margins are moving in favour of the banks, costs are under control and the sector will benefit from the new emerging customers. Profits should flow through to underpin current prices and we would still see the sector advancing further," he said.

Allardice also said that Old Mutual's Small Companies Fund, which holds stocks including financial services firm Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd and agricultural group OTK Holdings Ltd, had been showing excellent growth and attracting heavy investor interest.
On its Gold Fund, Allardice said that it would continue to try and beat the index by share selection.
"Primarily we focus within our gold fund on picking better gold shares which will be able to survive the gold price whether high or low," he said.
